name: Slack
description: Slack is a channel-based messaging platform. With Slack, people can work together more effectively, connect all their software tools and services, and find the information they need to do their best work - all within a secure, enterprise-grade environment.

tools.name: Add call participants
tools.description: Registers new participants added to a Slack call.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: ID of the call returned by the add method.

inputs.name: users
inputs.about: The list of users to add as participants in the call. users is a JSON array (formatted as a string) containing information for each user. Each element must include a `slack_id`. For example: `[{"slack_id": "U1H77"}]` or `[{"slack_id": "U1H77"}, {"slack_id": "U2ABC123"}]`.

tools.name: Add emoji
tools.description: Adds a custom emoji to a Slack workspace given a unique name and an image URL; subject to workspace emoji limits.

inputs.name: url
inputs.about: The URL of the image file to be used as the custom emoji. The image should be accessible via HTTP/HTTPS and meet Slack's emoji requirements (e.g., size, format). Supported formats typically include PNG, GIF, and JPEG.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The desired name for the new custom emoji. This name will be used to invoke the emoji (e.g., if name is 'partyparrot', it's used as ':partyparrot:'). Colons around the name are not required when providing this field. Must use lower-case letters only.

tools.name: Add an emoji alias
tools.description: Adds an alias for an existing custom emoji in a Slack Enterprise Grid organization.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The new alias to be created for the emoji specified in `alias_for` (e.g., `new_emoji_alias`). Colons around the name (e.g., `:my_alias:`) are optional and will be automatically trimmed, along with any leading/trailing whitespace.

inputs.name: alias_for
inputs.about: The canonical name of the existing custom emoji (e.g., `original_emoji`).

tools.name: Add Enterprise user to workspace
tools.description: Adds an Enterprise user to a workspace. Use when you need to assign an existing Enterprise Grid user to a specific workspace with optional guest restrictions.

inputs.name: team_id
inputs.about: The ID of the workspace (e.g., T1234567890) where the user will be added.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The ID of the user to add to the workspace.

inputs.name: channel_ids
inputs.about: Comma separated values of channel IDs to add user in the new workspace.

inputs.name: is_restricted
inputs.about: True if user should be added to the workspace as a guest. Guests can access only the channels they are invited to.

inputs.name: is_ultra_restricted
inputs.about: True if user should be added to the workspace as a single-channel guest. Single-channel guests can only access one channel (plus DMs and Huddles).

tools.name: Add reaction to message
tools.description: Adds a specified emoji reaction to a Slack message identified by channel and timestamp. An already-existing reaction is reported as success.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Name of the emoji to add as a reaction (e.g., 'thumbsup'). This is the emoji name without colons. For emojis with skin tone modifiers, append '::skin-tone-X' where X is a number from 2 to 6 (e.g., 'wave::skin-tone-3'). The emoji must already exist in the workspace; custom or non-existent emoji names

inputs.name: channel
inputs.about: ID of the channel where the message to add the reaction to was posted.

inputs.name: timestamp
inputs.about: Timestamp of the message to which the reaction will be added. This is a unique identifier for the message, typically a string representing a float value like '1234567890.123456'. Must be the exact message timestamp; permalinks or approximate values will not work.

tools.name: Add a remote file
tools.description: Adds a reference to an external file (e.g., Google Drive, Dropbox) to Slack for discovery and sharing, requiring a unique `external_id` and an `external_url` accessible by Slack.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: Title of the remote file to be displayed in Slack.

inputs.name: filetype
inputs.about: File type (e.g., 'pdf', 'docx', 'png') to help Slack display appropriate icons or previews.

inputs.name: external_id
inputs.about: Unique identifier for the file, defined by the calling application, used for future API references (e.g., updating, deleting).

inputs.name: external_url
inputs.about: Publicly accessible or permissioned URL of the remote file, used by Slack to access its content or metadata.

inputs.name: preview_image
inputs.about: Base64-encoded image (e.g., PNG, JPEG) used as the file's preview in Slack.

inputs.name: indexable_file_contents
inputs.about: Plain text content of the file, indexed by Slack for search.

tools.name: Add a star to an item
tools.description: Adds a star to a Slack channel, file, file comment, or message for the authenticated user. Stars added through this method can no longer be viewed or interacted with by end users.

inputs.name: file
inputs.about: ID of the file to add a star to.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.about: ID of the channel to star. If starring a specific message, this is the ID of the channel containing the message, and `timestamp` must also be provided.

inputs.name: timestamp
inputs.about: Timestamp of the message to add a star to. This uniquely identifies the message within the specified `channel`. Requires `channel` to also be provided.

inputs.name: file_comment
inputs.about: ID of the file comment to add a star to.

tools.name: Search for channels in Enterprise organization
tools.description: Tool to search for public or private channels in an Enterprise organization. Use when you need to find channels by name, type, or other criteria within an Enterprise Grid workspace.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: Sort method for channel search results.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Maximum number of items to be returned. Must be between 1 - 20 both inclusive. Default is 10.

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: Name of the channel to query by.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: Set cursor to next_cursor returned by the previous call to list items in the next page.

inputs.name: sort_dir
inputs.about: Sort direction for channel search results.

inputs.name: team_ids
inputs.about: Comma separated string of team IDs, signifying the workspaces to search through.

inputs.name: total_count_only
inputs.about: Only return the total_count of channels. Omits channel data and does not require full admin permissions.

inputs.name: connected_team_ids
inputs.about: Comma separated string of encoded team IDs, signifying the external organizations to search through.

inputs.name: search_channel_types
inputs.about: The type of channel to include or exclude in the search.

tools.name: Test Slack API connection
tools.description: Tool to check API calling code by testing connectivity and authentication to the Slack API. Use when you need to verify that API credentials are valid and the connection is working properly.

inputs.name: foo
inputs.about: Example property to return in the response. This can be any arbitrary string value to test echo functionality.

inputs.name: error
inputs.about: Error response to return. Use this parameter to test error handling by simulating various error responses.

tools.name: Archive a Slack conversation
tools.description: Archives a Slack conversation by its ID, rendering it read-only and hidden while retaining history, ideal for cleaning up inactive channels; be aware that some channels (like #general or certain DMs) cannot be archived and this may impact connected integrations.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.about: ID of the Slack conversation to archive. This ID uniquely identifies a channel (e.g., public, private).

tools.name: Real-time search
tools.description: Search Slack messages, files, channels, and users via the Real-time Search API, with content-type and conversation filters and pagination.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: Sort results by 'score' (relevance) or 'timestamp' (chronological). Defaults to score.

inputs.name: after
inputs.about: Unix timestamp. Only return results from after this date.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Maximum number of results per page. Max 20. Defaults to 20.

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: Search query. Supports both keyword search and natural language questions. Natural language queries (starting with what/where/how or ending with ?) trigger semantic search if available on the workspace. Supports OR operator for multiple terms: "deployment issues with kubernetes OR docker OR terrafor

inputs.name: before
inputs.about: Unix timestamp. Only return results from before this date.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.about: Pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor field.

inputs.name: sort_dir
inputs.about: Sort direction: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Defaults to desc.

inputs.name: highlight
inputs.about: Highlight matching search terms in the results.

inputs.name: modifiers
inputs.about: Additional search modifiers in 'modifier:value' format. E.g., 'has:pin before:yesterday is:thread'.

inputs.name: action_token
inputs.about: Action token from a Slack event payload. Required when using a bot token. Not needed for user tokens.

inputs.name: include_bots
inputs.about: Include bot messages in search results.

inputs.name: term_clauses
inputs.about: List of search term clauses for conjunctive matching. Results must match every clause specified. Each clause is a string with one or more search terms.

inputs.name: channel_types
inputs.about: Comma-separated channel types to include: public_channel, private_channel, mpim, im. Defaults to all channel types.

inputs.name: content_types
inputs.about: Comma-separated content types to search: messages, files, channels, users. Defaults to messages.

inputs.name: context_channel_id
inputs.about: Provide channel context for the search. Note: this parameter provides a contextual hint but may not strictly filter results to only this channel. To reliably restrict results to a specific channel, use the 'modifiers' parameter with 'in:channel_name' instead.

inputs.name: include_deleted_users
inputs.about: Include deleted users in search results. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: include_message_blocks
inputs.about: Return message blocks in the response.

inputs.name: disable_semantic_search
inputs.about: When true, forces keyword-only search even if the workspace has AI/semantic search available. Use this when SLACK_ASSISTANT_SEARCH_INFO returns is_ai_search_enabled=false, or when you explicitly want keyword matching.

inputs.name: include_context_messages
inputs.about: Include surrounding messages before and after each result for conversational context.

inputs.name: include_archived_channels
inputs.about: Include results from archived channels.

tools.name: Check search capabilities
tools.description: Check if semantic (AI-powered) search is available on the Slack workspace. Returns whether natural language queries will trigger semantic search in assistant.search.context calls.

tools.name: Send message
tools.description: Posts a message to a Slack channel, DM or private group using text, Markdown, blocks or attachments; this action is deprecated. Long converted Markdown may be split into threaded continuation messages, and a continuation failure can leave the initial message posted without all content.

inputs.name: text
inputs.about: DEPRECATED: This sends raw text only, use markdown_text field. Primary textual content. Recommended fallback if using `blocks` or `attachments`. Supports mrkdwn unless `mrkdwn` is `false`.

inputs.name: parse
inputs.about: Message text parsing behavior. Set to 'full' to parse as user-typed (auto-links @mentions, #channels). Omit for default behavior (no special parsing).

inputs.name: blocks
inputs.about: DEPRECATED: Use `markdown_text` field instead. Block Kit layout blocks for rich/interactive messages. Accepts either a URL-encoded JSON string or a list of block dictionaries. See Slack API Block Kit docs for structure.

inputs.name: mrkdwn
inputs.about: Controls Slack mrkdwn formatting for the top-level `text` field ONLY. Set to `false` to disable formatting (text appears as-is with literal asterisks, underscores, etc.). Default `true` enables mrkdwn formatting (*bold*, _italic_, etc.). NOTE: This parameter has NO effect on `blocks` or `markdown_te

inputs.name: channel
inputs.about: ID or name of the channel, private group, or IM channel to send the message to. Can be specified as either 'channel' or 'channel_id'. Do NOT include the '#' prefix (e.g., use 'general' not '#general') - any leading '#' will be automatically stripped. For DMs, use the channel ID returned by SLACK_OPE

inputs.name: thread_ts
inputs.about: Timestamp (`ts`) of an existing message to make this a threaded reply. Use `ts` of the parent message, not another reply. Example: '1476746824.000004'.

inputs.name: link_names
inputs.about: Automatically hyperlink channel names (e.g., #channel) and usernames (e.g., @user) in message text. Defaults to `false` for bot messages.

inputs.name: attachments
inputs.about: This is Slack's legacy 'secondary attachments' field for adding rich formatting elements like colored sidebars, structured fields, and author info to messages. Pass as a JSON string array. NOT for file/image uploads. To send a message with attachments of files or images, use the 'SLACK_UPLOAD_OR_CRE

inputs.name: unfurl_links
inputs.about: Enable unfurling of text-based URLs. Defaults `false` for bots, `true` if `as_user` is `true`.

inputs.name: unfurl_media
inputs.about: Enable media previews (images, videos) from URLs. Set to `true` (default) to show media previews, `false` to hide them.

inputs.name: markdown_text
inputs.about: PREFERRED: Write your message in markdown for nicely formatted display. Supports: headers (# ## ###), bold (**text** or __text__), italic (*text* or _text_), strikethrough (~~text~~), inline code (`code`), code blocks (```), links ([text](url)), block quotes (>), lists (- item, 1. item), dividers (-

inputs.name: reply_broadcast
inputs.about: If `true` for a threaded reply, also posts to main channel. Defaults to `false`.

tools.name: Close conversation channel
tools.description: Closes a Slack direct message (DM) or multi-person direct message (MPDM) channel, removing it from the user's sidebar without deleting history; this action affects only the calling user's view.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.about: The ID of the direct message or multi-person direct message channel to close. Example: D1234567890 or G0123456789.

tools.name: Complete external file upload
tools.description: Finalize uploaded file IDs once and optionally share the files.

inputs.name: files
inputs.about: One or more reserved Slack file IDs with optional titles.

inputs.name: blocks
inputs.about: Block Kit blocks for the file-share message; serialized for Slack, which ignores them when initial_comment is set.

inputs.name: channels
inputs.about: Comma-separated channel or user IDs where the files will be shared, up to 100 destinations.

inputs.name: thread_ts
inputs.about: Parent message timestamp when sharing the files as a thread reply.

inputs.name: channel_id
inputs.about: Channel where the completed files will be shared; omit to keep them private.

inputs.name: initial_comment
inputs.about: Comment introducing the shared files.

tools.name: Convert public channel to private
tools.description: Convert a public Slack channel to private using the Admin API. This is an Enterprise Grid only feature and requires an org-installed user token with admin.conversations:write scope.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Optional name parameter. Only respected when converting an MPIM (multi-person instant message).

inputs.name: channel_id
inputs.about: The ID of the public channel to convert to private. Required parameter.

tools.name: Create a reminder
tools.description: Creates a Slack reminder with specified text and time; time accepts Unix timestamps, seconds from now, or natural language (e.g., 'in 15 minutes', 'every Thursday at 2pm').

inputs.name: text
inputs.about: The textual content of the reminder message.

inputs.name: time
inputs.about: Specifies when the reminder should occur. This can be a Unix timestamp (integer, up to five years from now), the number of seconds until the reminder (integer, if within 24 hours, e.g., '300' for 5 minutes), or a natural language description (string, e.g., "in 15 minutes," or "every Thursday at 2pm"

inputs.name: user
inputs.about: The ID of the user who will receive the reminder (e.g., 'U012AB3CD4E'). If not specified, the reminder will be sent to the user who created it. NOTE: Setting reminders for other users is no longer supported for user tokens - only bot tokens can set reminders for other users.

inputs.name: team_id
inputs.about: ID of the Slack workspace (team) to operate on, e.g. T0123456789. Use only with org-level Enterprise Grid tokens when you need to target a specific workspace; omit for single-workspace tokens.

tools.name: Create Slack Canvas
tools.description: Creates a new Slack Canvas with the specified title and optional content.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the canvas to create. If not provided, Slack will generate a default title.

inputs.name: channel_id
inputs.about: Optional channel ID (e.g., 'C1234567890'). If provided, the canvas will be automatically added as a tab in this channel with write permissions.

inputs.name: document_content
inputs.about: Optional canvas content in Slack's document format. If not provided, creates an empty canvas.

tools.name: Create channel
tools.description: Initiates a public or private channel-based conversation in a Slack workspace. Immediately creates the channel; invoke only after explicit user confirmation.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Name of the public or private channel to create Must be lowercase, unique, and contain no spaces or periods; max 80 characters.

inputs.name: team_id
inputs.about: ID of the Slack workspace (team) to operate on, e.g. T0123456789. Use only with org-level Enterprise Grid tokens when you need to target a specific workspace; omit for single-workspace tokens.

inputs.name: is_private
inputs.about: Create a private channel instead of a public one

tools.name: Create a channel-based conversation
tools.description: Creates a new public or private Slack channel with a unique name; the channel can be org-wide, or team-specific if `team_id` is given (required if `org_wide` is false or not provided).

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Name for the new channel. Must be unique, 80 characters or fewer, lowercase, without spaces or periods, and may contain letters, numbers, and hyphens.

inputs.name: team_id
inputs.about: Workspace (team) ID for channel creation (e.g., T123ABCDEFG). Required if `org_wide` is `false` or not set.

inputs.name: org_wide
inputs.about: Set to `true` to make the channel available org-wide. If `false` or not set, `team_id` is required.

inputs.name: is_private
inputs.about: Set to `true` to make the channel private, or `false` for public.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Optional description for the channel (e.g., 'Discussion about Q4 marketing strategies').

tools.name: Create Enterprise team
tools.description: Tool to create an Enterprise team in Slack. Use when you need to create a new team (workspace) within an Enterprise Grid organization. Requires admin.teams:write scope.

inputs.name: team_name
inputs.about: Team name (for example, Slack Softball Team). This is the display name for the team.

inputs.name: team_domain
inputs.about: Team domain (for example, slacksoftballteam). This will be part of the team's URL.

inputs.name: team_description
inputs.about: Description for the team. Helps users understand the purpose of this team.

inputs.name: team_discoverability
inputs.about: Enum for team discoverability options.

tools.name: Create Slack List
tools.description: Creates a new Slack List via `slackLists.create`. Provide a `name` and, optionally, a `description_blocks` description and a `schema` of typed columns. You can instead copy an existing List's structure with `copy_from_list_id` (and its rows via `include_copied_list_records`), or enable task-tracking columns with `todo_mode`. Returns the new List's `list_id`. Requires a user token with the `lists:write` scope.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name (title) of the Slack List to create, e.g. 'Sprint Tasks'. This is shown as the List's title in Slack and is required.

inputs.name: schema
inputs.about: Column definitions for the List. Each entry is a column object describing a typed column (its `name`, `type`, and any type-specific options such as `select` choices). Supported column types include `text`, `select`, `user`, `date`, `number`, `checkbox`, and others. Omit to create a List with Slack's

inputs.name: todo_mode
inputs.about: Set to true to create the List in to-do mode, which adds Slack's built-in task-tracking columns (such as assignee, due date, and completion status) so the List behaves as a task tracker.

inputs.name: copy_from_list_id
inputs.about: ID of an existing Slack List to copy the structure from, e.g. 'F0123456789'. When provided, the new List is created with the same columns as that List. Use `include_copied_list_records` to also copy its rows.

inputs.name: description_blocks
inputs.about: Rich text describing the List, shown beneath the title. Slack stores this as Block Kit `rich_text` blocks. For convenience you may pass a plain string (it is wrapped into a `rich_text` block automatically), a single block dict (wrapped in a list), or an already-formed list of blocks (passed through

inputs.name: include_copied_list_records
inputs.about: When copying from another List via `copy_from_list_id`, set to true to also copy that List's existing items (rows) into the new List. Has no effect unless `copy_from_list_id` is set.

tools.name: Create Slack List item
tools.description: Creates a new item (row) in a Slack List via `slackLists.items.create`. Set initial cell values with `initial_fields`; text columns require Block Kit `rich_text` (a plain string is wrapped automatically). Optionally duplicate an existing row with `duplicated_item_id` or create a subtask with `parent_item_id`. Requires a user token with the `lists:write` scope.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: ID of the Slack List to add the item (row) to, e.g. 'F0123456789'. This is the List file ID returned by create_slack_list.

inputs.name: initial_fields
inputs.about: Initial cell values for the new row. Each entry is a cell object with a `column_id` and a typed value. Text columns must use Block Kit `rich_text` (the plain `text` property is not accepted on input) — for convenience a cell may instead supply a plain string `text` and it will be wrapped into a `ric

inputs.name: parent_item_id
inputs.about: ID of an existing item (row) to attach the new row to as a subtask. When provided, the new row is created as a sub-item of that parent.

inputs.name: duplicated_item_id
inputs.about: ID of an existing item (row) in this List to copy. When provided, the new row is created as a duplicate of that item; `initial_fields` may still be supplied to override copied values.

tools.name: Create a Slack user group
tools.description: Creates a new User Group (often referred to as a subteam) in a Slack workspace.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Unique name for the User Group. Must be unique among all User Groups in the workspace.

inputs.name: handle
inputs.about: Unique mention handle. Must be unique across channels, users, and other User Groups. Max 21 chars; lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores only.

inputs.name: team_id
inputs.about: ID of the Slack workspace (team) to operate on, e.g. T0123456789. Use only with org-level Enterprise Grid tokens when you need to target a specific workspace; omit for single-workspace tokens.

inputs.name: channels
inputs.about: Comma-separated encoded channel IDs for default channels, suggested when mentioning or inviting the group.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Short description for the User Group.

inputs.name: include_count
inputs.about: Include the User Group's user count in the response. Server defaults to `false` if omitted.

inputs.name: enable_section
inputs.about: Configure this user group to show as a sidebar section for all group members. Only relevant if group has 1 or more default channels added.

inputs.name: additional_channels
inputs.about: Comma-separated encoded channel IDs for which the User Group can custom add usergroup members to.

tools.name: Customize URL unfurl
tools.description: Customizes URL unfurls in a posted Slack message or message composer using custom preview content or Work Object metadata. It can also provide authentication prompts for unfurling.

inputs.name: ts
inputs.about: Timestamp of the message to customize URL unfurling for. Must be provided with `channel`, or alternatively provide `unfurl_id` and `source` together.

inputs.name: source
inputs.about: Link source: either 'composer' or 'conversations_history'. Must be provided with `unfurl_id`.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.about: Channel, private group, or DM channel to send message to. Can be an encoded ID, or a name. Must be provided with `ts`, or alternatively provide `unfurl_id` and `source` together.

inputs.name: unfurls
inputs.about: JSON string mapping URLs to custom unfurl content (Slack attachment format or blocks). Pass as a plain JSON string (not URL-encoded). To remove an existing unfurl, provide an empty object for that URL.

inputs.name: metadata
inputs.about: JSON object with 'entities' field providing Work Object array. Either `unfurls` or `metadata` is required. Pass as a JSON string.

inputs.name: unfurl_id
inputs.about: Link ID to unfurl. Must be provided with `source`. Alternative to using `channel` and `ts` parameters.

inputs.name: user_auth_url
inputs.about: URL-encoded custom URL for user authentication with your app to enable unfurling. Used when `user_auth_required` is true.

inputs.name: user_auth_blocks
inputs.about: JSON array of structured blocks (URL-encoded) sent as ephemeral authentication invitation. Alternative to `user_auth_message` for richer formatting. Used when `user_auth_required` is true.

inputs.name: user_auth_message
inputs.about: Ephemeral message text prompting user authentication with your app for domain-specific unfurling. Used when `user_auth_required` is true and authorization is pending.

inputs.name: user_auth_required
inputs.about: Set to `true` if user authentication is required to unfurl links for a domain, enabling an authentication flow using `user_auth_url` and `user_auth_message`.

tools.name: Delete Slack Canvas
tools.description: Deletes a Slack Canvas permanently and irreversibly; always confirm with the user before calling. For skill canvases, Slack may return success without deleting the canvas and indicate that the Skills API is required.

inputs.name: canvas_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the canvas to delete

tools.name: Delete a public or private channel
tools.description: Permanently and irreversibly deletes a specified public or private channel, including all its messages and files, within a Slack Enterprise Grid organization.

inputs.name: channel_id
inputs.about: ID of the channel to be permanently deleted. This channel can be public or private.

tools.name: Delete a file by ID
tools.description: Permanently deletes an existing file from a Slack workspace using its unique file ID; this action is irreversible and also removes any associated comments or shares.

inputs.name: file
inputs.about: ID of the file to delete. Typically obtained when a file is uploaded or listed.

tools.name: Delete file comment
tools.description: Deletes a specific comment from a file in Slack; this action is irreversible.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: ID of the comment to delete. This can be obtained when the comment is created or by listing file comments.

inputs.name: file
inputs.about: ID of the file to delete a comment from. The file ID can be obtained using the `files.info` method or when a file is shared.

tools.name: Delete multiple Slack List items
tools.description: Deletes several items (rows) from a Slack List in one call via `slackLists.items.deleteMultiple`. This operation is ALL-OR-NOTHING: Slack returns a single `{"ok": true}` on success or `{"ok": false, "error": ...}` on failure, with NO per-item result array, so partial state cannot be reported. On failure, treat the whole batch as not deleted and retry the entire batch. Requires a user token with the `lists:write` scope.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.about: Array of item (row) IDs to delete from the List in a single call, e.g. ['Rec0123456789', 'Rec9876543210']. IMPORTANT: this operation is ALL-OR-NOTHING. Slack `slackLists.items.deleteMultiple` returns a single `{"ok": true}` on success or `{"ok": false, "error": ...}` on failure, with NO per-item res

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: ID of the Slack List to delete items (rows) from, e.g. 'F0123456789'. This is the List file ID returned by create_slack_list. All of the `ids` must belong to this List.

tools.name: Delete a Slack reminder
tools.description: Deletes an existing Slack reminder, typically when it is no longer relevant or a task is completed; this operation is irreversible.

inputs.name: team_id
inputs.about: ID of the Slack workspace (team) to operate on, e.g. T0123456789. Use only with org-level Enterprise Grid tokens when you need to target a specific workspace; omit for single-workspace tokens.

inputs.name: reminder
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the reminder to be deleted. This ID is obtained when a reminder is created or listed.

tools.name: Delete a message from a chat
tools.description: Deletes a message, identified by its channel ID and timestamp, from a Slack channel, private group, or direct message conversation; the authenticated user or bot must be the original poster.

inputs.name: ts
inputs.about: Timestamp of the message to be deleted. Must be the exact Slack message timestamp string with fractional precision, e.g., '1234567890.123456'. Thread replies use their own `ts`; ephemeral messages and certain app-posted messages cannot be deleted via this method even with a valid timestamp.

inputs.name: as_user
inputs.about: Legacy parameter for classic Slack apps. Pass true to delete the message as the authed user. Bot tokens can only delete messages posted by that bot. This parameter is primarily for legacy apps and is generally not needed with modern bot tokens.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.about: The ID of the channel, private group, or direct message conversation containing the message to be deleted.

tools.name: Delete scheduled chat message

tools.name: Fetch conversation history

The oldest/latest timestamp filters work reliably for filtering the main channel timeline, but cannot be used to retrieve individual threaded replies - even if you know the exact reply timestamp, setting oldest=latest to that timestamp will return an empty messages array. To get threaded replies: 1. Use this action to get parent messages (which include thread_ts, reply_count, latest_reply fields) 2. Use SLACK_FETCH_MESSAGE_THREAD_FROM_A_CONVERSATION with the parent's thread_ts to fetch all replies in that thread

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Maximum number of messages to request in this single Slack API call (1-1000). Defaults to 100. inputs.name: latest

inputs.name: oldest
inputs.about: Start of the time range of messages to include in results. Accepts a Unix timestamp or a Slack timestamp (e.g., '1234567890.000000'). NOTE: This filter only applies to main channel messages, not threaded replies. Use SLACK_FETCH_MESSAGE_THREAD_FROM_A_CONVERSATION to retrieve replies.

inputs.name: channel

inputs.name: include_all_metadata
inputs.about: Return all metadata associated with messages in the conversation history. When true, includes additional metadata fields that may be present on messages.

tools.name: Set Slack List access
tools.description: Grants or sets sharing access on a Slack List via `slackLists.access.set`. Grant `read`, `write`, or `owner` access to either channels (`channel_ids`) or users (`user_ids`) — exactly one of the two is required. The `owner` level is user-only and subject to additional server-side rules. Requires a user token with the `lists:write` scope.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: ID of the Slack List to set sharing access on, e.g. 'F0123456789'. This is the List file ID returned by create_slack_list.

inputs.name: user_ids
inputs.about: IDs of the users to grant access to. Mutually exclusive with `channel_ids`: EXACTLY ONE of `channel_ids` or `user_ids` is required — supplying both or neither returns `invalid_parameters` from the API. Required when the `access_level` is `owner`.

inputs.name: channel_ids
inputs.about: IDs of the channels to grant access to. Mutually exclusive with `user_ids`: EXACTLY ONE of `channel_ids` or `user_ids` is required — supplying both or neither returns `invalid_parameters` from the API. Cannot be combined with the `owner` access level.

inputs.name: access_level
inputs.about: The access level to grant on the List. One of `read`, `write`, or `owner`. `read` grants view-only access; `write` grants edit access. `owner` is USER-ONLY: it must be paired with `user_ids` (not `channel_ids`) — supplying `channel_ids` together with `owner` returns `invalid_arguments` from the API.
